newsitem.title: MEXICO: Kennecott, Tayahua say signed Mexican mining deal.
newsitem.headline: Kennecott, Tayahua say signed Mexican mining deal.

text.p: Kennecott, a U.S. unit of Rio Tinto, and private Mexican miner Minera Tayahua SA said Tuesday they signed a joint venture called Kennecott Tayahua to operate Mexican mines.
Kennecott will take control of 65 percent of 16 of Tayahua's mines, the companies said in a statement.
Kennecott and Tayahua said that in three years they planned to raise total mining production to 30,000 tonnes from a current 2,500 tonnes per day.
"The operating plan established with Kennecott looks to expand proven reserves and raise processing volume in three years to a total 30,000 tonnes per day," the companies said.
The mines, in the central state of Zacatecas, have proven reserves of 60 million tonnes of copper, zinc, lead, gold and silver, the statement said. It did not provide a breakdown for each metal.
The companies said the transaction was worth $140 million, and that they planned to invest another $200 million in the next three years.
"The agreement...calls for a long term investment, which in its initial phase will be $200 million in three years," the firms said.

The companies said in a statement that the joint venture had been proposed a few years ago and was facilitated by Mexico's new mining legislation, which it said removed barriers to foreign investment.
Utah-based Kennecott is the U.S. subsidiary of the world's biggest miner Rio Tinto, formerly known as RTZ-CRA.
